newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CENTRAL BANK DRAFT BILL GOES TO PARLIAMENT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CENTRAL BANK DRAFT BILL GOES TO PARLIAMENT.

text.p: The government on Friday passed to parliament a proposal to revise legislation governing the Bank of Finland to bring it in line with requirements for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), the finance ministry said.

According to the proposal, the role in monetary and exchange rate policy decisions played by the central bank's board of parliamentary supervisors will cease once the new European central bank (ECB) is established, it said in a statement.
The ECB is scheduled to start operations in mid-1998, about half a year before the third phase of EMU is due to begin on January 1, 1997.

The government proposed that the legislative change could be approved by a simple majority in parliament, but it sought the constitutional committee's ruling on this, a senior finance ministry official said by telephone.
Parliament will start debating the proposal in February when it reconvenes after the Christmas recess.

Members of the Bank of Finland board of supervisors -- appointed by the political parties in proportion to their representation in parliament -- have earlier said they oppose being relieved of their role in exchange rate policy decision-making.
